_comment: A KEYM v3 container whose slot 0 declares 9,000,000 PBKDF2 iterations — inside
§6's ceiling of 10,000,000, so a reader must accept the slot and run the KDF.
The count was raised after the slot was sealed, so the wrap will not open and
the container will not decrypt. That is deliberate and irrelevant: §6 bounds-
checks the parameters and then derives, so the expensive part happens before
the reader can discover the slot is a dead end. What this fixture buys is a
derivation long enough to press Stop during, on a page with no Worker — the
one configuration where Stop cannot actually stop anything.
Argon2id will not do: on the main thread hash-wasm blocks the event loop, so
the button never renders. PBKDF2 goes through WebCrypto, off-thread, and
leaves the tab responsive — which is exactly why the wording matters there.
